newsitem.title: USA: Armey says encouraged about U.S. budget prospects.
newsitem.headline: Armey says encouraged about U.S. budget prospects.

text.p: House Majority Leader Dick Armey said Wednesday "there were encouraging signs" that Republicans would reach a budget deal with the White House.

Speaking to reporters, Armey said he had every reason to believe that the White House was "clearly and sincerely" trying to reach a deal, but said again that Republicans would move forward with their own plan if no agreement was reached.
He said again that he did not believe Congress ought to legislate changes to the Consumer Price Index as part of a budget deal, calling it a technical issue that should be left up to the experts.

Many economists believe the CPI overstates inflation. Because automatic cost of living increases in many federal programs are tied to the CPI, an adjustment could save the government tens of billions of dollars.
"I don't believe in legislating technical matters," he said.
